facts.fact_text: The applicant, together with another person, intended to organise demonstrations to draw attention to the situation of those having foreign currency loans.
The applicant, together with another person, intended to organise demonstrations to draw attention to alleged fraudulent banking policies.
The applicant, together with another person, intended to organise demonstrations to put pressure on decision-makers so that respect for the rule of law gains primacy over the interests of oligarchs.
On 8 December 2014 the applicant notified the Budapest police department of his intention to organise a demonstration.
The demonstration was scheduled for 19 December 2014 between 9 a.m. and 8 p.m.

The demonstration was planned to take place at nine venues: the headquarters of different banks, the Israeli embassy, the Kúria, the home of the chief executive officer (CEO) of the biggest commercial bank in Hungary, the home of the prime minister, and the Offices of the National Assembly.
The demonstration was planned to include a march between the different locations.
The organisers specified that it was expected that about thirty to one hundred persons would participate in the demonstration.
The organisers specified that it was expected that about twenty to fifty cars would participate in the demonstration.
